title: Notebook: base64 image output, cell ids and execution metadata
summary: A synthetic notebook with a markdown cell, a code cell with a UUID-shaped cell id, execution timestamps and a tag in cell metadata, and a display_data output holding a 48x48 PNG as a base64 list of lines, a text/plain label and a +json MIME entry holding ordinary values. Nothing in it is a credential.
rationale: A saved notebook is full of long, random-looking strings by design: base64 image data declared by its MIME key, cell ids of 1 to 64 identifier characters, ISO 8601 timestamps. Failure mode: treating declared image data or identifier metadata as a credential because it is long and high entropy. The specification states what each field is, but does not say that none of them can hold a secret, and a decoded image or a free-form metadata value could in principle carry one; so the neutral expectation is not asserted from the specification alone. The PNG was built by an authored description (a fixed pseudo-random pixel generator, zlib, valid chunk checksums) and holds no text.
unscopedReason: The values belong to the notebook file format, not to a credential family; the control is meant to apply to every family.

expectation.rationale: Not asserted. The notebook format documents image/png data as base64-encoded PNG data, a cell id as a 1 to 64 character string of letters, digits, hyphen and underscore, and execution timestamps as ISO 8601 values, so each value's role is documented. None of the sources states that these values are not credentials, and ADR 0019 (items 1 and 8) does not accept a role description as evidence of non-secrecy, so a neutral expectation here would need a maintainer decision with a non-author reviewer. A maintainer may decide must-not-flag as project-policy; until then the fixture records the input and its documented roles, with no spans. Resolving needs a maintainer decision, not more reading.

sources.supports: display_data data may hold image/png as base64-encoded multiline PNG data; metadata.image/png carries width and height.
Since nbformat 4.5 every cell has an id of 1-64 characters from alphanumerics, hyphen and underscore, unique within the notebook.
Cell metadata execution.iopub.execute_input and related keys hold ISO 8601 times of kernel messages; tags is a list of strings.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
